curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `iw aw iW aW`; `i" a"`, `i' a'`, ``i` a` ``; `i( a(`, `i) a)`, `ib ab`; `i[ a[`, `i] a]`; `i{ a{`, `i} a}`, `iB aB`; `i< a<`, `i> a>`; `is as`, `ip ap`, `it at`
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Choose inside versus around and apply any learned operator to a structural object
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Change a quoted value; delete function arguments; replace an object literal; nest a list block; remove a tag element with its markup; finish an item retrieved by search
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core. Tag and angle-bracket objects are exercised only where the buffer makes their boundaries unambiguous, and angle-bracket objects are marked advanced

lessons.title: Choose contents or surroundings
lessons.objective: Use inside and around word objects with previously learned operators.

activities.title: Text objects select complete pieces of text
activities.body: A text object selects a complete item around the cursor, such as a word or quoted text. Use `i` for only the contents, or `a` to include the surrounding quotes, brackets, or nearby space.
activities.contrast: A motion travels somewhere; a text object describes what to act on.

activities.contrast: Sentence objects are characterwise; paragraph objects commonly become linewise ranges.

activities.title: Indent one paragraph
activities.instruction: Nest the whole middle block of items one level deeper, without touching the blocks around it.

commandGroups.explanation: Indent every line of the block the cursor sits in.

hints: The block runs from the cursor's line to the next blank line.
Give the indent operator a paragraph object rather than a line count.
Press `>ip`.

feedback.success: All three items in the block are nested, and the neighbouring blocks are untouched.
feedback.why: `ip` measured the block from its blank-line boundaries, so the operator covered every row without you counting them.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; the app fixes the indentation unit at two spaces.

provenance.languageRationale: A Markdown list long enough to run past the window shows the object covering rows a line operator would have to count.

activities.title: Remove a paragraph and separator
activities.instruction: Remove the whole block of draft notes along with the blank line that follows it.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete the block and the blank line that separates it from the next one.

hints: The block is three rows long and is followed by a blank line.
Around a paragraph includes that trailing blank line; inside it does not.
Press `dap`.

feedback.success: The draft block is gone and the remaining blocks are still separated correctly.
feedback.why: `ap` took the trailing blank line with the block, so no stray separator was left behind.

provenance.languageRationale: Release notes long enough to run past the window make the removed block and its separator both visible.

lessons.title: Target balanced HTML elements
lessons.objective: Replace tag contents or include the enclosing tags.

activities.title: Select the contents or whole HTML tag
activities.body: Use `it` to select the content between matching opening and closing tags, however many rows it covers. Use `at` to include both tags and everything between them.
activities.contrast: Use `it` to preserve markup; use `at` to move or remove the entire element. Neither needs a line count: the object finds the matching close for you.

activities.title: Empty an element that spans rows
activities.instruction: Clear everything inside the list element while leaving the list itself in place.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete everything between the enclosing tag's open and close.

checkpoints.caption: Four rows collapsed into one; both tags survived.

hints: The enclosing element is the list, not one of its items.

feedback.success: All three items are gone and the list element is still there.
feedback.why: The object reached from the opening tag to its matching close — past the bottom of the window — without you counting a single row.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior on balanced lowercase HTML tags.

provenance.languageRationale: A list whose items continue below the window is the case a line count would get wrong.

activities.title: Replace tag contents
activities.instruction: Change the heading text to “Ready”, leaving its tags in place.

commandGroups.explanation: Change everything between the enclosing tag's open and close.

hints: Only the text between the tags changes.
Use the inside form of the tag object.
Press `citReady` then `Esc`.

feedback.success: The heading reads Ready and both tags survived.
feedback.why: Inside a tag stops at the tags themselves, so the markup was never at risk.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior on balanced lowercase HTML tags.

provenance.languageRationale: A single-line heading isolates the inside-versus-around choice before the multi-row cases.

activities.title: Capture an element with its markup
activities.instruction: Capture the heading element complete with its opening and closing tags.

commandGroups.explanation: Yank the enclosing element together with its opening and closing tags.

hints: The tags belong to the capture this time.
Use the around form of the tag object.
Press `yat`.

feedback.success: The complete element, tags included, was captured.
feedback.why: Around a tag reaches from the `<` of the opening tag to the `>` of the closing one, so the markup travels with the text.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior on balanced lowercase HTML tags.

provenance.languageRationale: A single-line heading isolates the around reading from any question of how many rows are involved.

activities.title: Remove one item outright
activities.instruction: Remove the first list item entirely, its markup included, leaving the other two.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete the enclosing element together with its tags.

hints: The item's tags have to go as well, so inside is the wrong reading.
The cursor is already within the item; the object finds its boundaries.
Press `dat`.

feedback.success: The item and both of its tags are gone.
feedback.why: The object covered the element but not the indentation in front of it, which is why the row is left blank rather than removed.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior on balanced lowercase HTML tags.

provenance.languageRationale: One item among three shows the element boundary precisely, including the indentation the object leaves behind.

lessons.title: Choose the object, then the operator
lessons.objective: Transfer operator grammar across words, delimiters, quotes, prose, and tags.

activities.title: Use text objects with any operator
activities.body: Choose an operator such as delete, change, or copy. Then choose `i` for the contents or `a` for the surroundings, and finish with the object name.
activities.contrast: Prefer the smallest object that states the intended boundary clearly.

activities.title: Choose inside, then around
activities.instruction: Capture just the arguments, then remove the arguments together with their parentheses.

commandGroups.explanation: Delete the same structure including its parentheses.

checkpoints.caption: Around takes the delimiters with it.

hints: The same object answers to two different questions.

feedback.success: One structure, two ranges, two different results.
feedback.why: Inside and around name the same object; only the delimiters decide which of the two you get.

provenance.languageRationale: One call expression carries both readings of the same object without any other structure competing.

activities.title: Replace a whole object literal
activities.instruction: Replace the options object, braces and all, with “null”.

commandGroups.explanation: Change the brace object including its braces.

hints: The braces have to go as well, so inside is the wrong reading.
Compose the change operator with the around form of the brace object.
Press `ca{null` then `Esc`.

feedback.success: The object literal was replaced outright.
feedback.why: Because the braces were part of the replacement, `a{` was the only reading that covered the whole value.

provenance.languageRationale: Replacing a configuration object with a single value is the case that forces the around reading.

activities.title: Find the pending item and finish it
activities.instruction: Locate the item still marked pending, below the window, and change its text to “Docs ready”.

commandGroups.explanation: Enter the text to search for.
Run the search and scroll the match into view.
Change the contents of the tag the match landed in.

checkpoints.caption: The search reached a row that was below the window.

hints: The item is not on screen; retrieve it rather than scrolling to it.
Once the search lands inside the item, the enclosing tag is the object you want.
Search for the word, then change inside the tag.

feedback.success: The item off screen was found and finished in one pass.
feedback.why: Search carried the cursor into the element, and the tag object then described the edit without any counting.

activities.portability: Core Vim behavior; the app parses the complete HTML buffer so the closing tag is resolved beyond the cursor.

provenance.languageRationale: A list continuing below the window makes retrieval a real requirement rather than a decoration.

activities.title: Structures are reusable ranges
activities.body: You can now apply familiar operators to words, quotes, balanced delimiters, prose blocks, and HTML elements.
takeaways: Choose inside when boundaries should remain.
Choose around when delimiters or separator whitespace belong to the edit.
Compose operators with objects instead of counting characters.
